text:
elaine: quick follow-up from the cp split spike — proposal: introduce a lightweight 'tombstone' marker for controlplane-local endpoint records + a lease-sweep job that clears tombstones after a grace TTL. aim: avoid stale route flaps during cross-region detach/onboard races.

samir: high level — tombstone lives in the same k/v store as the endpoint entry? or separate namespace?

elaine: keep same store but different key suffix: `endpoint/<tenant>/<id>#tombstone` so reads are single-prefix scans. not adding another service.

matt: how does this interact with routing decisions? if relay sees tombstone should it fall back to global-relay immediately or wait for sweep?

elaine: relay logic: if tombstone exists and tombstone_ts + tombstone_ttl < now => treat as deleted (fall back). if tombstone exists but within grace => prefer local with degraded penalty. prevents instant flap while detach propagates.

olga: what's the proposed grace TTL? minutes or hours?

elaine: default 5m, configurable per-tenant. idea: short enough to not mask real deletes, long enough for peering/route reconvergence (we measured ~90s on most peering flows).

chen: concern: split-brain where two CPs think they own the endpoint and write/delete rapidly — tombstone could keep bouncing. how do we pick authoritative writer?

samir: we already have cp-lease-holder metadata (owner region + epoch). tombstone write must include owner epoch. lease-sweep verifies epoch consistency before clearing tombstone. if owner epoch changed, tombstone gets extended or becomes immutable until resolved.

matt: can we see a sample tombstone payload?

elaine: sure — sample: 
```json
{"owner":"cp-us-west-2","owner_epoch":1534,"tombstone_ts":1690000000,"reason":"customer-detach","meta":"route-evict"}
```
keep payload compact.

olga: sweep job rules? who runs it and how often?

elaine: background job in controlplane-local (cron) runs every 30s per region, does prefix scan for `#tombstone` keys with tombstone_ts + ttl < now, then attempts a CAS delete only if owner_epoch matches. emits metrics `tombstone.sweeps`, `tombstone.gc.failures`.

chen: CAS required to avoid races with re-onboard during sweep. what about retries/backoff?

samir: job should use exponential backoff on CAS failures and cap attempts (3). we should also emit a debug log with keys failing after attempts for human ops.

matt: storage cost? scans at scale could be heavy for big tenants with many endpoints. we have to avoid full-table scans.

elaine: we only scan tombstone-prefixed keys (same prefix as endpoints). tombstone density expected low — typical tenants won't tombstone more than N endpoints at once. if we see pathological tenants we rate-limit sweeps per-tenant.

olga: observability — add a new alert for tombstone growth rate (sustained > 5/min) and sweep backlog > 1m keys.

chen: downgrade plan — if sweep job fails for >10m, fallback: signal global-relay to treat tombstones as stale and prefer global routing. ensures availability.

matt: one more: KV cache (clients hold endpoint KV in memory). how do we ensure cache invalidation when tombstone gets created?

elaine: publish tombstone events on existing ephemeral watch stream. clients must subscribe to `endpoint/*` prefix; watch event types: `PUT`, `DELETE`, `TOMBSTONE`. clients treat `TOMBSTONE` similar to `DELETE` but with grace window info included so they can continue degraded behaviour.

samir: can we reuse existing watch codec? adding `TOMBSTONE` should be backwards-compatible; older clients will treat it as PUT (still ok) but we should roll new client bump for better behaviour.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: `deploy/cp-local-tombstone 2026-03-22T10:54Z by elaine` :rocket:

olga: ops checklist before rollout? testing items: race test with dual-writes, sweep load test, watch fanout latency test, metric alert thresholds tuned.

elaine: yep — I'll put up a short spike PR with tests + perf numbers. if no objections we'll schedule a staged rollout to us-west then eu-central.

matt: +1 from runtime side. please include a config flag to disable tombstones per-tenant for early beta.

chen: also document expected semantics in controlplane contract doc (small section). saves support confusion.

samir: one nit — name it `tombstone` or `soft-delete`? `tombstone` reads nicer in logs. :shrug:

elaine: we'll go with `tombstone` for the key suffix and `soft-delete` in user-facing docs.

olga: thanks — tagging infra for rollout runbook: @infra-oncall

infra-bot: @infra-oncall notified for runbook review.

elaine: thanks everyone. I'll post the PR link here when ready. :+1:
